status_definitions.stable: End-to-end product surface with automated regression evidence and supported upgrade semantics.
status_definitions.beta: Usable end-to-end surface with known limitations; API or behavior may still change.
status_definitions.experimental: Partial or opt-in implementation that is not part of the supported product contract.
status_definitions.planned: Accepted direction without a supported implementation.

capabilities.name: Issue management
capabilities.summary: Workspace-scoped issue CRUD, assignment, comments, timeline, reactions, and subscribers.

capabilities.name: Local agent runtime
capabilities.summary: Local daemon claims tasks and runs supported coding-agent CLIs.
limitations: Provider capability conformance and deeper Windows process-tree cancellation tests are not yet release gates.

capabilities.name: Truthful CLI command surface
capabilities.summary: The registered Cobra tree is the single source for no-argument and --help output, while exact English and Chinese top-level command inventories are enforced by contract tests.
limitations: The guides document common workflows and the complete top-level inventory; detailed nested flags remain generated by each command's --help output.

capabilities.name: Realtime workspace sync
capabilities.summary: WebSocket broadcasts synchronize workspace entities and task lifecycle events; owner/admin-authenticated cloud gateways stream redacted logs through a durable cursor ledger with bounded Web snapshots and reconnect recovery.
limitations: Realtime fanout is still single-server and in-memory; sticky-free multi-replica delivery remains M7-02.

capabilities.name: Task graph
capabilities.summary: Issue-scoped DAG visualization, persisted nodes and edges, and node mutation APIs.
limitations: Task graph nodes are planning artifacts; Agentra does not automatically schedule, execute, recover, or hand off graph nodes.

capabilities.name: Goal to DAG auto-decomposition
capabilities.summary: A planner decomposes an issue description into a persisted task graph.
limitations: Golden-repository outcome evaluation is not yet enforced.

capabilities.name: Engineering loop
capabilities.summary: Plan, develop, review, fix, and verify stages coordinate iterative engineering work.
limitations: Loop and task-graph lifecycle models are not yet unified.

capabilities.name: Agent and team memory
capabilities.summary: Workspace-scoped agent and team memory CRUD with a Web viewer and BM25 search across team plus non-private agent records.
limitations: Create flows currently store zero-vector placeholders; semantic/vector retrieval is not a supported surface.
There is no wired graph, temporal, RRF, or automatic task-context injection path.
BM25 currently uses PostgreSQL's english text-search configuration; multilingual recall quality is not yet a supported contract.
Provenance, TTL, confidence, PII handling, and prompt-injection policy are incomplete.

capabilities.name: Execution traces
capabilities.summary: Task execution trace records are persisted and retrievable through backend APIs.
limitations: There is no supported Web trace viewer; the disconnected legacy UI was removed rather than preserving an incompatible API path.

capabilities.name: Agent task metrics
capabilities.summary: Owner/admin-only workspace aggregates expose provider and task performance metrics.
limitations: The route is mounted, but end-to-end authorization and dashboard regression coverage are incomplete.

capabilities.name: Projects and milestones
capabilities.summary: Workspace-scoped project and milestone management with a routed Web experience for project creation, issue assignment, status updates, and deletion.
limitations: Project lead, progress, resources, and richer planning fields are not yet implemented.
Project mutations are limited to workspace owners and admins.

capabilities.name: MCP server
capabilities.summary: A policy-scoped MCP server will expose Agentra work operations to compatible agent clients.

capabilities.name: Cloud runtime
capabilities.summary: A gateway can execute dispatched tasks in managed containers.
limitations: Live log delivery, recovery semantics, and production isolation are incomplete.

capabilities.name: Agentra Eval harness
capabilities.summary: The CLI validates the 25-case static fixture contract and labels its output as a non-gating fixture check.
limitations: No agent is executed, so fixture matches are not implementation-quality measurements.
There is no supported Eval HTTP or Web surface and no release regression gate.
A real benchmark still needs isolated repositories, observable diff/test/lint outcomes, repeated samples, and a durable execution ledger.

capabilities.name: Runtime adapter conformance
capabilities.summary: A versioned fixture suite will certify provider capabilities and platform behavior.

capabilities.name: Self-host health probes
capabilities.summary: Separate liveness and readiness endpoints report database, migration, configured object storage, and scheduler health for self-hosted deployments.
limitations: Readiness does not yet cover realtime fanout, outbound email, or cloud gateway capacity.
N-1 migration rehearsal and Kubernetes packaging are not release gates yet.

capabilities.name: Self-host installation diagnostics
capabilities.summary: A bounded diagnostic command checks configuration security, Web/API readiness, storage, authentication, workspace access, runtime CLIs, filesystem and Git permissions, local daemon health, and authenticated WebSocket ping/pong.
limitations: The storage diagnosis uses server readiness rather than performing an object write/delete smoke.
Repository access validates origin HEAD and local write permissions but does not test push authorization.

capabilities.name: Guided machine setup
capabilities.summary: A single idempotent command preflights cloud or self-hosted readiness, Web access, and local coding-agent CLIs, authenticates, discovers workspaces, and starts the profile-isolated daemon.
limitations: A public Agentra Cloud endpoint is not released, so cloud setup requires explicit HTTPS URLs.
The command assumes the CLI is already installed; the first public release with verifiable macOS/Linux/Windows artifacts requires the next tag.

capabilities.name: Cross-platform CLI installers
capabilities.summary: Homebrew, checksum-verifying macOS/Linux shell installation, and Windows PowerShell installation are generated from one GoReleaser contract with native CI fixtures.
limitations: The Homebrew cask and Windows archive become publicly available only after the next tagged release runs the updated pipeline.
The installers enforce SHA-256 locally; independent Cosign and GitHub provenance verification remains an explicit user step.
An obsolete formula remains in the external tap until the cask migration is completed during release.

capabilities.name: Unified release metadata
capabilities.summary: One checked release metadata document drives package versions, release tags, CLI/server/gateway build info, the public version API, Web build metadata, README, and Roadmap claims.
limitations: The next tagged release must run the updated workflows before publicly distributed CLI and container artifacts satisfy this contract.
Direct local development builds intentionally report dev/unknown instead of pretending to be the current release.

capabilities.name: Verifiable release supply chain
capabilities.summary: Tagged CLI releases and multi-architecture GHCR images are built with SPDX SBOMs, identity-bound Cosign keyless signatures, and GitHub artifact provenance from pinned workflows.
limitations: The first public assets satisfying this contract require the next v* tag; older GitHub Releases and Docker Hub images are outside it.
Installers enforce SHA-256 but require users to invoke Cosign or GitHub CLI explicitly for workflow-identity verification.
macOS code signing/notarization and Windows Authenticode are not yet implemented.

capabilities.name: Secure self-host bootstrap
capabilities.summary: A non-overwriting bootstrap generates independent PostgreSQL, JWT, and MinIO credentials with owner-only permissions; Compose fails closed on missing secrets and hides data/admin surfaces by default.
limitations: Secure environment bootstrap currently targets bash on macOS/Linux; an equivalent PowerShell bootstrap remains planned.
Kubernetes/Helm secret references and external secret-manager integrations are not yet packaged.

capabilities.name: Policy-controlled email authentication
capabilities.summary: Email OTP delivery supports Resend and SMTP with enforced TLS modes, while server-side signup allowlists and workspace-creation policy preserve invitation-only deployments.
limitations: Email and access policy configuration is process-wide and requires a server restart to change.
SMTP protocol behavior is unit-tested but not yet exercised against provider containers in CI.
Readiness does not yet probe outbound email delivery, and the Web UI does not expose policy administration.

capabilities.name: Durable automations
capabilities.summary: Cron, webhook, manual, and VCS triggers will share an idempotent admission and run model.
